extracted.intended_audience: nonprofit communications staff, marketers, and communications directors
extracted.subtask_description: Practical guidelines for writing, packaging, and distributing press releases for nonprofit organizations, emphasizing stakeholder relevance, measurable impact, multimedia, and coordinated cross-channel distribution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mobile-first audience
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognize that your audience is mobile-first.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Write and format releases for readability on mobile devices (short paragraphs, scannable headings, mobile-friendly assets). Ensure links, images, and attachments work well on phones.

rubrics_metrics.name: Social media as primary discovery channel
rubrics_metrics.description: Treat social media as a primary way people discover your news.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Craft copy and assets tailored for social sharing (snappy pull-quotes, images, short video). Use social channels to amplify the release rather than relying solely on traditional pickups.

rubrics_metrics.name: Email newsletter as relationship builder
rubrics_metrics.description: Use your email newsletter to build relationships and share news directly with supporters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include the release or a tailored summary in newsletters to reach engaged audiences who may act (donate, volunteer, attend). Coordinate timing between the release and newsletter send.

rubrics_metrics.name: Press release as one tool among many
rubrics_metrics.description: A press release is one tool in an integrated communications toolkit, not the only tactic.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plan releases as part of broader campaigns that include social, email, partner outreach, and earned media strategies. Don't expect a release alone to achieve all goals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cross-channel coordination
rubrics_metrics.description: Coordinate the release across channels for maximum reach and consistency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure messaging, visuals, calls-to-action, and timing align across local press outreach, sector publications, wire services, social media, email, and partner shares.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stakeholder relevance (The Stakeholder Test)
rubrics_metrics.description: Demonstrate that the news matters to key stakeholders: donors, beneficiaries, volunteers, the broader community, and peer nonprofits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicitly answer who cares and why — tailor the angle or data to each stakeholder group when possible. Use this test before issuing a release to avoid sending non-news.

rubrics_metrics.name: Single clear call-to-action (The Action Test)
rubrics_metrics.description: Define one clear action you want readers to take (donate, volunteer, attend, share).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid multiple conflicting CTAs. State the desired action clearly in the release and ensure links/buttons lead directly to the action (donation page, sign-up form, event registration).

rubrics_metrics.name: Impact reporting with specific metrics
rubrics_metrics.description: Report impact using specific, measurable metrics rather than vague claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include numbers, outcomes, timelines, and methodology where relevant. Avoid generic phrases like 'transformed lives' without support. Specific metrics increase credibility and newsworthiness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Campaign launches should include goals
rubrics_metrics.description: When announcing a campaign launch, include clear goals and targets.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State fundraising or programmatic goals, timelines, and what success will look like to make the story concrete and actionable for readers and reporters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Beneficiary stories with permission
rubrics_metrics.description: Use beneficiary stories only when you have explicit consent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Obtain written permission for quotes, photos, and identifying information. Protect privacy and dignity; consider anonymizing sensitive cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Partner announcements
rubrics_metrics.description: Announce partnerships clearly, explaining roles and outcomes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe who the partners are, what each contributes, and the expected impact. Coordinate messaging and approvals with partner organizations before distribution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Crisis response
rubrics_metrics.description: Use the release format appropriately for crisis communications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritize timely, factual information and next steps. Be transparent about actions taken, who is affected, and how stakeholders can get help or more information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Annual reports and major gift recognition
rubrics_metrics.description: Use releases for annual report highlights and major gift announcements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Highlight measurable outcomes, donor intent (with permission), and how the gift will be used. Tie announcements to broader impact and next steps for beneficiaries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Headline: impact-first, not mission-first
rubrics_metrics.description: Write headlines that lead with impact rather than organizational mission statements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Frame the headline around what changed or what will happen (e.g., 'Organization X helps 1,000 families secure housing') rather than 'Organization X celebrates...' which is less newsy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lede: who, what, when, where, why, how
rubrics_metrics.description: Open with a lede that covers the essential journalism questions: who, what, when, where, why, and how.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make the most newsworthy element clear in the first paragraph so journalists and readers immediately understand the story's relevance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Body: methodology, quotes, proof points
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide supporting details in the body: methods, credible proof points, and illustrative quotes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain how impact was measured, include data or third-party validation, and use quotes to humanize and substantiate claims. Avoid unsupported assertions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quotes from beneficiary and leadership
rubrics_metrics.description: Include at least one quote from a beneficiary and one from organizational leadership.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Beneficiary quotes provide human impact; leadership quotes provide context and organizational perspective. Ensure beneficiary consent and authenticity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Boilerplate: mission, scale, impact metrics
rubrics_metrics.description: End with a boilerplate that succinctly states your mission, organizational scale, and key impact metrics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep the boilerplate factual and concise so journalists can easily lift standard background information for their stories.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contact information for communications staff
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide a named communications staff member as the media contact.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include direct phone, email, and availability. Make it easy for reporters to reach someone for follow-up and interviews.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multimedia required (photos, infographics)
rubrics_metrics.description: Include multimedia assets such as photos and infographics to strengthen the story.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Multimedia increases pick-up and social sharing. Provide high-resolution images, captions, and usage permissions. Use infographics to illustrate impact metrics clearly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Photos of beneficiaries with consent
rubrics_metrics.description: Use photos of beneficiaries only with consent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Obtain written permission and inform subjects how and where photos will be used. Be sensitive to dignity and privacy concerns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Video testimonials when possible
rubrics_metrics.description: Include video testimonials to add immediacy and emotional resonance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Short, captioned videos work well on social platforms and news sites. Secure releases for likeness and consider accessibility (captions, transcripts).

rubrics_metrics.name: Before/after images and impact maps
rubrics_metrics.description: Use before/after images and impact maps to visualize change and geographic reach.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Visuals that show comparison or geographic scope can make abstract impact more tangible for audiences and reporters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Local press first
rubrics_metrics.description: Prioritize outreach to local media outlets before wider distribution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Local outlets are more likely to pick up community-focused stories; tailor pitches to local angles and contacts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sector publications second
rubrics_metrics.description: Pitch sector- or issue-specific publications after local outreach.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Target trade and nonprofit-sector media with specialized angles relevant to their audiences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Wire syndication for SEO
rubrics_metrics.description: Consider wire distribution to improve SEO and broader visibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use wire services strategically; wire syndication can help with discoverability but should be coordinated with targeted outreach.

rubrics_metrics.name: Social media amplification
rubrics_metrics.description: Amplify the release via social media channels.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use platform-appropriate copy and assets, schedule posts to match audience habits, and encourage partners and staff to share.

rubrics_metrics.name: Email newsletter inclusion
rubrics_metrics.description: Include the release or a summary in your email newsletter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tailor the message for subscribers and link directly to the action you want them to take.

rubrics_metrics.name: Partner organization sharing
rubrics_metrics.description: Ask partner organizations to share the release to expand reach.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Coordinate timing and provide assets and suggested language to make sharing easy for partners.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid excessive mission language (anti-pattern)
rubrics_metrics.description: Don't lead with mission statements or organizational self-promotion instead of news.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Journalists and audiences seek newsworthy changes or impacts; excessive mission language reduces newsworthiness and should be minimized.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid beneficiary stories without permission (anti-pattern)
rubrics_metrics.description: Never publish beneficiary stories, quotes, or images without explicit consent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lack of permission can cause ethical issues, legal risk, and harm to beneficiaries. Consent procedures should be standard.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid vague impact claims (anti-pattern)
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid vague, unsupported claims such as 'transformed lives'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Substantiate impact statements with data, examples, or methodology. Vague claims undermine credibility and reduce pickup.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid releasing without multimedia (anti-pattern)
rubrics_metrics.description: Releases without any multimedia are less likely to be picked up or shared.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include at least one strong image or infographic; where possible add video to increase engagement.

rubrics_metrics.name: News-cycle awareness
rubrics_metrics.description: Be aware of the news cycle and time releases strategically.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid sending releases into news deserts (major breaking news moments, holidays) and aim for times when reporters are most receptive; coordinate timing with partners and channels.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality Rubric (aggregate checklist)
rubrics_metrics.description: A concise checklist summarizing the key quality dimensions: stakeholder relevance demonstrated; single clear call-to-action; specific impact metrics; multimedia (photos, infographics); beneficiary voice with consent; cross-channel coordination; news-cycle awareness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this checklist as a pre-release QA step to ensure the release meets nonprofit best-practice standards before distribution.
